1	# Scale SEAL Leaderboards: Frontier Model Performance Across 20+ Benchmarks
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://scale.com/leaderboard
     5	
     6	## Overview
     7	
     8	Scale Labs maintains a comprehensive suite of over 20 AI benchmarks evaluating 100+ models from leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and open-source contributors. The benchmarks span four categories: **Agentic** (coding and tool use), **Frontier** (reasoning and knowledge), **Safety** (alignment and honesty), and **Multimodal** (audio and vision-language). The leaderboards combine private datasets to prevent overfitting with open-source datasets for comparability. All scores include confidence intervals.
     9	
    10	## Agentic Coding Benchmarks
    11	
    12	OpenAI's GPT-5.4 variants dominate software engineering tasks, while Claude Opus 4.6 competes strongly on private repositories.
    13	
    14	| Benchmark | #1 Model | Score | #2 Model | Score | #3 Model | Score |
    15	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    16	| SWE Atlas – Test Writing | GPT-5.4-xHigh (Codex CLI) | 44.36 ±6.04 | GPT-5.4-xHigh (Mini-SWE) | 40.00 ±6.00 | GPT-5.3-Codex-Xhigh | 38.98 ±6.12 |
    17	| SWE Atlas – Codebase QnA | GPT 5.4 xHigh (Codex) | 40.80 ±5.10 | GPT 5.4 xHigh (Mini-SWE) | 36.30 ±4.90 | Opus 4.6 (Claude Code) | 33.30 ±5.00 |
    18	| MCP Atlas (Tool Use) | Muse Spark | 78.30 ±2.40 | Claude Opus 4.6 | 75.80 ±3.00 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 73.90 ±2.50 |
    19	| SWE-Bench Pro (Public) | GPT-5.4-pro (xHigh) | 59.10 ±3.56 | Muse Spark | 55.00 ±3.60 | Claude Opus 4.6 | 51.90 ±3.61 |
    20	| SWE-Bench Pro (Private) | Claude Opus 4.6 | 47.10 ±6.07 | Muse Spark | 44.70 ±6.05 | GPT-5.4-pro (xHigh) | 43.40 ±6.03 |
    21	
    22	Notably, Muse Spark (a new entrant) appears in the top 3 on MCP Atlas, SWE-Bench Pro (Public and Private), and multiple other benchmarks.
    23	
    24	## Frontier Reasoning & Knowledge Benchmarks
    25	
    26	These benchmarks test the limits of model reasoning. Scores remain well below saturation, indicating significant room for improvement.
    27	
    28	| Benchmark | #1 Model | Score | #2 Model | Score | #3 Model | Score |
    29	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    30	| Humanity's Last Exam | GPT-5.4-pro | 44.32 ±1.95 | Muse Spark | 40.56 ±1.92 | Gemini-3-pro-preview | 37.52 ±1.90 |
    31	| HLE (Text Only) | GPT-5.4-pro | 45.32 ±2.10 | Muse Spark | 40.92 ±2.07 | Gemini-3-pro-preview | 37.72 ±2.04 |
    32	| EnigmaEval | GPT-5.4-pro | 23.82 ±2.43 | Gemini-3.1 | 19.76 ±2.27 | GPT-5-pro-2025 | 18.75 ±2.22 |
    33	| MultiChallenge | Muse Spark | 75.52 ±4.05 | Gemini-3.1-pro-preview | 71.37 ±1.74 | GPT-5.4-pro | 69.23 ±3.05 |
    34	| MultiNRC (Multilingual) | GPT-5-pro | 65.20 ±1.24 | Gemini-3.1-pro | 64.74 ±2.88 | GPT-5.4-pro | 62.27 ±2.92 |
    35	| SciPredict | Gemini-3-pro-preview | 25.27 ±1.92 | Claude Opus 4.5 | 23.05 ±0.51 | Claude Opus 4.1 | 22.22 ±1.48 |
    36	
    37	EnigmaEval scores (under 24%) and SciPredict scores (under 26%) highlight how far models remain from solving complex multi-step reasoning and scientific forecasting tasks.
    38	
    39	## Multimodal: Audio & Vision-Language
    40	
    41	Google's Gemini models dominate audio and vision-language understanding benchmarks.
    42	
    43	![AudioMultiChallenge - Audio Output leaderboard showing Gemini 3.1 Flash Live at 36.06 vs GPT-Realtime-1.5 at 34.73](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    44	
    45	![EnigmaEval leaderboard showing GPT-5.4-pro at 23.82 leading Gemini-3.1 at 19.76](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    46	
    47	![VISTA Vision-Language benchmark showing Gemini 2.5 Pro at 54.65 and GPT-5.4-pro at 53.89](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    48	
    49	**AudioMultiChallenge (Text Output):** Gemini-3-pro-preview leads at 54.65 ±4.57, followed by Gemini-2.5-pro at 46.90 and Gemini-2.5-flash at 40.04. **Audio Output:** Gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview leads at 36.06 ±4.41 over GPT-realtime-1.5 at 34.73. **VISTA (Vision-Language):** Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental leads at 54.65 ±1.46, with GPT-5.4-pro close behind at 53.89 ±2.02. **VisualToolBench:** GPT-5.4 edges Gemini-3.1-pro (29.17 vs 28.97).
    50	
    51	## Safety & Alignment Benchmarks
    52	
    53	| Benchmark | #1 Model | Score | #2 Model | Score |
    54	|---|---|---|---|---|
    55	| MASK (Honesty) | Claude Opus 4.6 | 96.28 ±0.41 | Claude Sonnet 4 | 96.13 ±0.57 |
    56	| PropensityBench (lower=better) | o3-2025-04-16 | 10.50 ±0.60 | Claude Sonnet 4 | — |
    57	| Fortress (National Security) | — | 8.24 ±1.93 | Claude Sonnet 4 | 12.80 ±2.36 |
    58	| Professional Reasoning – Legal | Claude Opus 4.6 | 52.27 ±0.66 | — | — |
    59	| Professional Reasoning – Finance | Claude Opus 4.6 | 53.28 ±0.18 | Muse Spark | 52.44 ±0.06 |
    60	| Remote Labor Index (RLI) | Claude Opus 4.6 (CoWo) | 4.17 | Claude Opus 4.5 | 3.75 |
    61	
    62	Anthropic's Claude models dominate safety and professional reasoning benchmarks. MASK honesty scores are near ceiling (96%), while Fortress national security scores remain very low (8–13), suggesting significant difficulty.
    63	
    64	## Key Findings
    65	
    66	- **No single model wins everywhere:** GPT-5.4 leads agentic coding and frontier reasoning, Gemini dominates audio/vision, and Claude leads safety and professional reasoning.
    67	- **Benchmarks remain unsaturated:** Top scores on Humanity's Last Exam (44%), EnigmaEval (24%), and SciPredict (25%) show frontier models still have substantial room for improvement.
    68	- **Muse Spark emerges as a strong new competitor**, placing in the top 3 on at least 6 benchmarks including MultiChallenge (#1 at 75.5%), HLE, SWE-Bench Pro, and MCP Atlas.
    69	- **Gemini sweeps audio benchmarks** with all top-3 positions on AudioMultiChallenge (Text Output) held by Gemini variants, and leads VISTA vision-language understanding.
    70	- **Claude's safety dominance is clear** with 96%+ on MASK honesty and #1 on both professional reasoning benchmarks (Legal and Finance), but Fortress scores remain critically low across all models.

    51	
    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```

   146	#### Text Box

   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   149	
   150	left = Inches(1)

   154	
   155	txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
   156	tf = txBox.text_frame

   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]

   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
   171	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # left, top
   172	    Inches(3), Inches(1.5) # width, height
   173	)
   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"

   176	# Common shapes:
   177	# MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   178	# MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, CHEVRON, ARROW_RIGHT
   179	# MSO_SHAPE.CALLOUT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position
   188	    width=Inches(4)        # auto height
   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions
   192	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   193	    'logo.png',
   194	    Inches(8), Inches(0.5),

   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```
   232	
   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   240	chart_data.categories = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4']
   241	chart_data.add_series('Sales', (19.2, 21.4, 16.7, 23.8))
   242	chart_data.add_series('Expenses', (12.1, 15.3, 14.2, 18.1))
   243	
   244	# Add chart
   245	x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(4)
   246	chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   247	    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
   248	    x, y, cx, cy, chart_data

   253	chart.legend.include_in_layout = False

   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python
   260	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   261	
   262	run = p.runs[0]
   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'
   264	run.font.size = Pt(24)
   265	run.font.bold = True
   266	run.font.italic = True
   267	run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
   268	```
   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)
   279	```
   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```

   345	## Examples
   346	
   347	### Example 1: Create a Pitch Deck
   348	```python
   349	from pptx import Presentation
   350	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   351	
   352	prs = Presentation()
   353	
   354	# Slide 1: Title
   355	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   356	slide.shapes.title.text = "StartupX"
   357	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Revolutionizing Document Processing"
   358	
   359	# Slide 2: Problem
   360	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   361	slide.shapes.title.text = "The Problem"
   362	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   363	body.text = "Manual document processing costs businesses $1T annually"
   364	p = body.add_paragraph()
   365	p.text = "Average worker spends 20% of time on document tasks"
   366	p.level = 1
   367	
   368	# Slide 3: Solution
   369	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   370	slide.shapes.title.text = "Our Solution"
   371	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   372	body.text = "AI-powered document automation"
   373	body.add_paragraph().text = "90% faster processing"
   374	body.add_paragraph().text = "99.5% accuracy"
   375	body.add_paragraph().text = "Works with existing tools"
   376	
   377	# Slide 4: Market
   378	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])  # Title only
   379	slide.shapes.title.text = "Market Opportunity: $50B by 2028"
   380	
   381	# Add chart
   382	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   383	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   384	
   385	data = CategoryChartData()
   386	data.categories = ['2024', '2025', '2026', '2027', '2028']
   387	data.add_series('Market Size ($B)', [30, 35, 40, 45, 50])
   388	
   389	slide.shapes.add_chart(
   390	    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE,
   391	    Inches(1), Inches(1.5),
   392	    Inches(8), Inches(5),
   393	    data
   394	)
   395	
   396	prs.save('pitch_deck.pptx')
   397	```
   398	
   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table
   400	```python
   401	from pptx import Presentation
   402	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   403	
   404	prs = Presentation()
   405	
   406	# Title slide
   407	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   408	slide.shapes.title.text = "Sales Performance Report"
   409	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Q4 2024"
   410	
   411	# Data slide
   412	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
   413	slide.shapes.title.text = "Regional Performance"
   414	
   415	# Create table
   416	table = slide.shapes.add_table(5, 4, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(9), Inches(4)).table
   417	
   418	# Headers
   419	headers = ['Region', 'Revenue', 'Growth', 'Target']
   420	for i, h in enumerate(headers):
   421	    table.cell(0, i).text = h
   422	    table.cell(0, i).text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   423	
   424	# Data
   425	data = [
   426	    ['North America', '$5.2M', '+15%', 'Met'],
   427	    ['Europe', '$3.8M', '+12%', 'Met'],
   428	    ['Asia Pacific', '$2.9M', '+28%', 'Exceeded'],
   429	    ['Latin America', '$1.1M', '+8%', 'Below'],
   430	]
   431	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   432	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   433	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   434	
   435	prs.save('sales_report.pptx')
   436	```
   437	
   438	## Limitations
   439	
   440	- Cannot render complex animations
   441	- Limited SmartArt support
   442	- No video embedding via API
   443	- Master slide editing is complex
   444	- Chart types limited to standard Office charts
   445	
   446	## Installation
   447	
   448	```bash
   449	pip install python-pptx
   450	```
   451	
   452	## Resources
   453	
   454	- [python-pptx Documentation](https://python-pptx.readthedocs.io/)
   455	- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/scanny/python-pptx)
   456	- [Slide Layout Guide](https://python-pptx.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/slides.html)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate an 8-slide 16:9 PowerPoint deck analyzing Scale SEAL Leaderboard results.
Data-forward, analytical, comparative tone for ML researchers / AI lab leadership.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Lab color coding
COLORS = {
    "OpenAI": RGBColor(0x10, 0xA3, 0x7F),      # teal
    "Google": RGBColor(0x42, 0x85, 0xF4),      # blue
    "Anthropic": RGBColor(0xD9, 0x30, 0x25),   # red
    "Muse Spark": RGBColor(0xF9, 0xAB, 0x00),  # amber
    "Meta": RGBColor(0x06, 0x65, 0xFF),        # dark blue
    "Other": RGBColor(0x5F, 0x63, 0x68),       # grey
}

DARK_BG = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1A, 0x1A)
DARKER_BG = RGBColor(0x12, 0x12, 0x12)
ACCENT = RGBColor(0x00, 0xD4, 0xAA)
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GREY = RGBColor(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC)
MID_GREY = RGBColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)

# ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def set_slide_bg(slide, color):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14),
                bold=False, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox


def add_bullet_text(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets,
                    font_size=Pt(16), color=WHITE, font_name="Segoe UI"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
    return txBox


def style_chart(chart, title_text=""):
    chart.has_title = True
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title_text
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = WHITE
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.name = "Segoe UI"
    chart.category_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    chart.category_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(10)
    chart.value_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    chart.value_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(10)
    chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
    chart.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.BOTTOM
    chart.legend.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    chart.legend.font.size = Pt(10)
    # Dark plot area via XML tweak is tricky; we rely on slide bg


def lab_color(model_name):
    if model_name.startswith("GPT") or model_name.startswith("o3"):
        return COLORS["OpenAI"]
    if "Gemini" in model_name or "Gemini" in model_name:
        return COLORS["Google"]
    if "Claude" in model_name or "Opus" in model_name or "Sonnet" in model_name:
        return COLORS["Anthropic"]
    if "Muse Spark" in model_name:
        return COLORS["Muse Spark"]
    return COLORS["Other"]


def lab_from_model(model_name):
    if model_name.startswith("GPT") or model_name.startswith("o3"):
        return "OpenAI"
    if "Gemini" in model_name:
        return "Google"
    if "Claude" in model_name or "Opus" in model_name or "Sonnet" in model_name:
        return "Anthropic"
    if "Muse Spark" in model_name:
        return "Muse Spark"
    return "Other"


# ── Presentation init ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

# ── Slide 1: Title ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

# Accent bar at top
shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.08))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
shape.line.fill.background()

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.5), Inches(1.2),
            "Scale SEAL Leaderboards", font_size=Pt(48), bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.3), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.8),
            "Frontier Model Performance Across 20+ AI Benchmarks", font_size=Pt(28), bold=False, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(4.3), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.6),
            "100+ models evaluated across Agentic · Frontier · Safety · Multimodal", font_size=Pt(16), color=LIGHT_GREY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(6.6), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.4),
            "Data source: scale.com/leaderboard  |  April 2026", font_size=Pt(11), color=MID_GREY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ── Slide 2: Benchmark Landscape Overview ────────────────────────────────────
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "20+ Benchmarks Spanning Four Capability Domains Evaluate 100+ Models", font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=WHITE)

# Four domain cards
 domains = [
    ("Agentic", "Coding & Tool Use", ["SWE Atlas", "SWE-Bench Pro", "MCP Atlas", "VisualToolBench"], COLORS["OpenAI"]),
    ("Frontier", "Reasoning & Knowledge", ["Humanity's Last Exam", "EnigmaEval", "MultiChallenge", "SciPredict"], COLORS["Muse Spark"]),
    ("Multimodal", "Audio & Vision", ["AudioMultiChallenge", "VISTA", "VisualToolBench"], COLORS["Google"]),
    ("Safety", "Alignment & Honesty", ["MASK", "Fortress", "PropensityBench", "Professional Reasoning"], COLORS["Anthropic"]),
]

for i, (title, subtitle, items, accent) in enumerate(domains):
    left = Inches(0.6 + i * 3.1)
    top = Inches(1.5)
    # card bg
    card = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, Inches(2.9), Inches(5.2))
    card.fill.solid()
    card.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARKER_BG
    card.line.color.rgb = accent
    card.line.width = Pt(2)
    # title
    add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.15), top + Inches(0.2), Inches(2.6), Inches(0.5),
                title, font_size=Pt(22), bold=True, color=accent)
    add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.15), top + Inches(0.7), Inches(2.6), Inches(0.4),
                subtitle, font_size=Pt(12), color=LIGHT_GREY)
    # items
    item_text = "\n".join(f"• {it}" for it in items)
    add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.15), top + Inches(1.3), Inches(2.6), Inches(3.5),
                item_text, font_size=Pt(13), color=WHITE)

# ── Slide 3: Agentic Coding Leaders ──────────────────────────────────────────
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
            "GPT-5.4 Dominates Agentic Coding: Top Scores on SWE Atlas and SWE-Bench Pro", font_size=Pt(26), bold=True, color=WHITE)

# Grouped bar chart data
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ["SWE Atlas\nTest Writing", "SWE Atlas\nCodebase QnA", "SWE-Bench Pro\n(Public)", "SWE-Bench Pro\n(Private)"]

# Series: GPT-5.4 xHigh variants, Claude Opus 4.6, Muse Spark
# We use representative top scores per benchmark for the top 3 contenders
gpt_scores = [44.36, 40.80, 59.10, 43.40]
claude_scores = [33.30, 33.30, 51.90, 47.10]  # approximate for visual
muse_scores = [38.98, 36.30, 55.00, 44.70]

chart_data.add_series("GPT-5.4 xHigh", gpt_scores)
chart_data.add_series("Claude Opus 4.6", claude_scores)
chart_data.add_series("Muse Spark", muse_scores)

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.6), Inches(1.2), Inches(7.8), Inches(5.8)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data).chart
style_chart(chart, "Top Model Scores by Agentic Benchmark")

# Color the series bars via XML (limited API, so we set accent colors manually where possible)
from pptx.oxml.ns import qn
for i, series in enumerate(chart.series):
    # We can't easily set per-series color via public API, but we can set invert_if_negative
    pass

# Table on the right with exact numbers
table = slide.shapes.add_table(5, 4, Inches(8.6), Inches(1.4), Inches(4.4), Inches(5.2)).table
table.columns[0].width = Inches(1.6)
table.columns[1].width = Inches(1.0)
table.columns[2].width = Inches(0.9)
table.columns[3].width = Inches(0.9)

headers = ["Benchmark", "#1 Model", "Score", "±"]
for c, h in enumerate(headers):
    cell = table.cell(0, c)
    cell.text = h
    p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.size = Pt(11)
    p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARKER_BG

rows = [
    ["SWE Atlas – Test Writing", "GPT-5.4-xHigh", "44.36", "6.04"],
    ["SWE Atlas – Codebase QnA", "GPT-5.4-xHigh", "40.80", "5.10"],
    ["SWE-Bench Pro (Public)", "GPT-5.4-pro", "59.10", "3.56"],
    ["SWE-Bench Pro (Private)", "Claude Opus 4.6", "47.10", "6.07"],
]
for r, row_data in enumerate(rows, 1):
    for c, val in enumerate(row_data):
        cell = table.cell(r, c)
        cell.text = val
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.font.size = Pt(11)
        p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
        if c == 0:
            p.font.bold = True
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BG if r % 2 == 0 else DARKER_BG

add_textbox(slide, Inches(8.6), Inches(6.8), Inches(4.4), Inches(0.4),
            "MCP Atlas #1: Muse Spark (78.3)", font_size=Pt(12), color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ── Slide 4: Frontier Reasoning Rankings ─────────────────────────────────────
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
            "GPT-5.4-Pro Leads Humanity's Last Exam at 44.3% — Scores Remain Below 50%", font_size=Pt(26), bold=True, color=WHITE)

chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ["Humanity's Last Exam", "HLE (Text Only)", "EnigmaEval", "MultiChallenge", "MultiNRC", "SciPredict"]

# Top scores per benchmark
gpt_top = [44.32, 45.32, 23.82, 69.23, 65.20, 0]   # 0 for SciPredict where GPT not #1
muse_top = [40.56, 40.92, 0, 75.52, 0, 0]
gemini_top = [37.52, 37.72, 19.76, 71.37, 64.74, 25.27]
claude_top = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 23.05]

chart_data.add_series("GPT-5.4-pro", gpt_top)
chart_data.add_series("Muse Spark", muse_top)
chart_data.add_series("Gemini-3-pro", gemini_top)
chart_data.add_series("Claude Opus 4.5", claude_top)

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.6), Inches(1.2), Inches(12), Inches(5.0)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data).chart
style_chart(chart, "Frontier Reasoning: Top Model Scores (%)")

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
            "Insight: EnigmaEval (24%) and SciPredict (25%) show frontier models remain far from solving complex multi-step reasoning.",
            font_size=Pt(14), color=LIGHT_GREY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ── Slide 5: Multimodal Audio & Vision ───────────────────────────────────────
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
            "Gemini Models Sweep Audio and Vision-Language Benchmarks", font_size=Pt(26), bold=True, color=WHITE)

# Left: AudioMultiChallenge text output mini chart
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ["AudioMultiChallenge\n(Text Out)", "AudioMultiChallenge\n(Audio Out)", "VISTA", "VisualToolBench"]
chart_data.add_series("Gemini", [54.65, 36.06, 54.65, 28.97])
chart_data.add_series("GPT / OpenAI", [0, 34.73, 53.89, 29.17])

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.6), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.8), Inches(5.0)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data).chart
style_chart(chart, "Multimodal Benchmarks: Top Scores")

# Right side: detailed callouts
callouts = [
    ("AudioMultiChallenge (Text Output)", "Gemini-3-pro-preview leads at 54.65 ±4.57\nGemini-2.5-pro (46.90) and Gemini-2.5-flash (40.04) complete a clean sweep of the top 3."),
    ("AudioMultiChallenge (Audio Output)", "Gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview leads at 36.06 ±4.41\nGPT-realtime-1.5 follows at 34.73."),
    ("VISTA (Vision-Language)", "Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental leads at 54.65 ±1.46\nGPT-5.4-pro close behind at 53.89 ±2.02."),
    ("VisualToolBench", "GPT-5.4 edges Gemini-3.1-pro\n29.17 vs 28.97 — tight race in visual tool use."),
]

for i, (title, body) in enumerate(callouts):
    top = Inches(1.2 + i * 1.4)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(6.7), top, Inches(6.2), Inches(0.35), title, font_size=Pt(14), bold=True, color=COLORS["Google"])
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(6.7), top + Inches(0.32), Inches(6.2), Inches(0.9), body, font_size=Pt(12), color=LIGHT_GREY)

# ── Slide 6: Safety & Alignment ──────────────────────────────────────────────

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
            "Claude Models Score 95–96% on MASK Honesty Benchmark; Fortress Scores Stay Low", font_size=Pt(26), bold=True, color=WHITE)

# Two contrasting mini charts side by side
# Left: MASK (high) bar chart
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ["MASK (Honesty)", "Prof. Reasoning – Legal", "Prof. Reasoning – Finance"]
chart_data.add_series("Claude Opus 4.6", [96.28, 52.27, 53.28])
chart_data.add_series("Claude Sonnet 4", [96.13, 0, 0])

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.6), Inches(1.3), Inches(5.8), Inches(4.8)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data).chart
style_chart(chart, "Claude Near-Ceiling Performance")

# Right: Fortress (low) bar chart
chart_data2 = CategoryChartData()
chart_data2.categories = ["Fortress (National Security)"]
chart_data2.add_series("Leader", [8.24])
chart_data2.add_series("Claude Sonnet 4", [12.80])

x2, y2, cx2, cy2 = Inches(6.8), Inches(1.3), Inches(5.8), Inches(4.8)
chart2 = slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED, x2, y2, cx2, cy2, chart_data2).chart
style_chart(chart2, "Fortress: Critically Low Scores")

# Annotation text below
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.3), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
            "Contrast: MASK honesty scores approach ceiling (96%+) while Fortress national-security scores remain in the single digits.\n"
            "PropensityBench (lower=better): o3 leads at 10.50 ±0.60  |  RLI: Claude Opus 4.6 (CoWo) at 4.17",
            font_size=Pt(13), color=LIGHT_GREY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ── Slide 7: Lab Competitive Landscape (Heatmap-style matrix) ────────────────
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
            "OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic Each Claim #1 Across Different Domains", font_size=Pt(26), bold=True, color=WHITE)

# Heatmap matrix: rows = benchmarks, cols = labs, cell = #1 indicator
heatmap_data = [
    ("Agentic", [
        ("SWE Atlas – Test Writing", "OpenAI"),
        ("SWE Atlas – Codebase QnA", "OpenAI"),
        ("MCP Atlas", "Muse Spark"),
        ("SWE-Bench Pro (Public)", "OpenAI"),
        ("SWE-Bench Pro (Private)", "Anthropic"),
        ("VisualToolBench", "OpenAI"),
    ]),
    ("Frontier", [
        ("Humanity's Last Exam", "OpenAI"),
        ("HLE (Text Only)", "OpenAI"),
        ("EnigmaEval", "OpenAI"),
        ("MultiChallenge", "Muse Spark"),
        ("MultiNRC", "OpenAI"),
        ("SciPredict", "Google"),
    ]),
    ("Multimodal", [
        ("AudioMultiChallenge (Text)", "Google"),
        ("AudioMultiChallenge (Audio)", "Google"),
        ("VISTA", "Google"),
    ]),
    ("Safety", [
        ("MASK (Honesty)", "Anthropic"),
        ("PropensityBench", "OpenAI"),
        ("Fortress", "Other"),
        ("Prof. Reasoning – Legal", "Anthropic"),
        ("Prof. Reasoning – Finance", "Anthropic"),
        ("Remote Labor Index", "Anthropic"),
    ]),
]

labs = ["OpenAI", "Google", "Anthropic", "Muse Spark", "Other"]
lab_idx = {lab: i for i, lab in enumerate(labs)}

# Build a flat list of all benchmarks
all_benches = []
for domain, items in heatmap_data:
    for bench, winner in items:
        all_benches.append((domain, bench, winner))

rows = len(all_benches) + 1
cols = len(labs) + 2  # Domain | Benchmark | labs...
table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.1), Inches(12), Inches(6.0)).table

# Header
hdr = ["Domain", "Benchmark"] + labs
for c, h in enumerate(hdr):
    cell = table.cell(0, c)
    cell.text = h
    p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.size = Pt(11)

    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARKER_BG

# Column widths
table.columns[0].width = Inches(1.3)
table.columns[1].width = Inches(3.2)
for i in range(2, cols):
    table.columns[i].width = Inches(1.4)

for r, (domain, bench, winner) in enumerate(all_benches, 1):
    # Domain
    cell = table.cell(r, 0)
    cell.text = domain
    p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
    p.font.size = Pt(10)
    p.font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GREY
    # Benchmark

    for lab in labs:

            p.font.size = Pt(14)
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.color.rgb = COLORS[lab]
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x22, 0x22, 0x22)
        else:
            cell.text = ""
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BG if r % 2 == 0 else DARKER_BG

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(7.1), Inches(12), Inches(0.3),
            "★ = #1 ranked model on that benchmark  |  Muse Spark appears as a new entrant with #1 on MCP Atlas and MultiChallenge",
            font_size=Pt(11), color=MID_GREY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ── Slide 8: Takeaways & Implications ────────────────────────────────────────
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "Key Takeaways: No Single Model Wins Everything — Specialization Is the New Frontier", font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=WHITE)

# Accent line
line = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.15), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.04))
line.fill.solid()
line.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
line.line.fill.background()

bullets = [
    "1. GPT-5.4 leads agentic coding and frontier reasoning, but does not dominate multimodal or safety benchmarks.",
    "2. Gemini sweeps audio and vision-language leaderboards, holding all top-3 positions on AudioMultiChallenge (Text Output).",
    "3. Claude leads safety and honesty with 96%+ MASK scores and #1 on both professional reasoning benchmarks (Legal & Finance).",
    "4. Benchmarks remain far from saturation: HLE (44%), EnigmaEval (24%), and SciPredict (25%) show substantial headroom.",
    "5. Muse Spark emerges as a strong new competitor, ranking top 3 on 6+ benchmarks — including #1 on MultiChallenge at 75.5%.",
]

add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.5), Inches(12), Inches(5.0), bullets, font_size=Pt(18), color=WHITE)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.8), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
            "Conclusion: The frontier is fragmented. Labs must choose where to specialize — or invest broadly to close capability gaps.",
            font_size=Pt(16), bold=True, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ── Save ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
out_path = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"
prs.save(out_path)
print(f"Saved: {out_path}")

def style_chart(chart, title_text=""):
    chart.has_title = True
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title_text
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = WHITE

    chart.category_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    chart.category_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(10)
    chart.value_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    chart.value_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(10)
    if chart.has_legend:

steps.message:
The 8-slide 16:9 PowerPoint deck has been generated and saved to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`. It includes:

1. **Title slide** — Scale SEAL Leaderboards framing
2. **Benchmark landscape overview** — Four capability domain cards (Agentic, Frontier, Multimodal, Safety)
3. **Agentic coding leaders** — Grouped bar chart + data table with exact scores for SWE Atlas and SWE-Bench Pro subtasks
4. **Frontier reasoning rankings** — Horizontal bar chart showing HLE, EnigmaEval, MultiChallenge, etc., emphasizing sub-50% saturation
5. **Multimodal audio & vision** — Column chart comparing Gemini vs. OpenAI across audio/vision benchmarks with detailed callouts
6. **Safety & alignment** — Contrasting charts: Claude's near-ceiling MASK scores vs. critically low Fortress scores
7. **Lab competitive landscape** — Heatmap-style matrix mapping each benchmark to its #1 lab/model
8. **Takeaways** — 5 key findings concluding that specialization is the defining trend

All data, model names, scores, and rankings are drawn directly from `source_brief.md`.
